gtk.title: Pushchairs and buggies
gtk.text: I can’t find any rule against pushchairs, and there’s baby changing next to the toilets. It’s mostly grass and a long walk from the car parks, so I would bring one with chunky wheels.

gtk.title: Dogs
gtk.text: Only assistance dogs are allowed, and that includes leaving pets in the car. I would leave yours at home with someone you trust, as an airfield is no place for them.

gtk.title: Your own food and drink
gtk.text: Picnics are welcome, but cooking equipment and barbecues aren’t allowed. The rules I read don’t say either way about alcohol, so I would check with the show before you pack any.

gtk.title: Gazebos, windbreaks and chairs
gtk.text: Folding chairs are fine. Shelters and step ladders up to 1.5 metres are allowed, but not within 10 metres of the crowd line, and tents aren’t allowed along it.

gtk.title: Water refill points
gtk.text: I haven’t seen free water points confirmed for Cosford. I would bring plenty of your own, as there is very little shade on the crowd line.

gtk.title: Changing Places toilet
gtk.text: There are disabled toilets across the showground. The museum has a Changing Places toilet in its Visitor Centre on normal days, so I would ask the show whether you can use it on air show day.

gtk.title: Carers' tickets
gtk.text: Qualifying disabled visitors can bring a registered carer free of charge, but conditions apply. I would sort this out when you book, as nothing is sold at the gate.

gtk.title: Hearing support (hearing loops, BSL, deaf visitors)
gtk.text: I haven’t seen hearing loops or BSL confirmed for the air show itself. I would contact the show before you go, so you know what to expect on the day.

gtk.title: Quiet area (a calm or sensory space)
gtk.text: There’s no quiet area confirmed on the showground. The museum has quiet rooms on normal days, and its hangars are a good place to get away from the noise for a bit.

gtk.title: Re-entry (can you leave and come back)
gtk.text: The rules I read don’t cover re-entry. If you think you’ll need to pop back to the car, I would ask the show before you go, as it’s a long walk each way.

gtk.title: First aid and lost children
gtk.text: There are medical facilities across the site, and any steward can point you to the nearest one. Under 16s must be with an adult, so I would agree a meeting point before you go in. There’s more in Help on show days.

gtk.title: If it rains
gtk.text: Unfortunately the weather on the day will be what it will be, so plan accordingly. If it’s fresh, dress in layers to keep warm. If the flying is cut back, aircraft may be taxied instead, and there are no refunds.

ground.html:
The Ground Show

Gates open hours before the first display, and I would make the most of that time. Cosford’s static park is a bit special, because a lot of it comes from the station itself. You get the training airframes the RAF engineers learn on, aircraft from the museum and visitors from other air forces, all on one airfield.

CostIncluded in your ticket
GatesOpen 08:00 (2026)
FlyingFrom about 11:30
BringCash, just in case

How I Would Do It

  1. Save your pitch firstIf you want a front row seat, head to the crowd line as soon as you’re in and set up your chairs or blanket. Then you can explore without worrying.
  2. Walk the static park earlyBefore 10:00 it’s much quieter. That’s the time to take a look around, speak to the pilots and crews and get photos without people in the way.
  3. Then the hangars and stallsVisit the STEM hangars, the RAF stands and the trade stalls, and check the food options while the queues are short.
  4. Toilet before the flyingI would go before the flying display starts. Later on, if you aren’t waiting to see a particular display, use it as a toilet break.

Things To See

Included

The Static Park

In 2026 it had Jaguars, Hawks, Tornados and Wessex helicopters from the station’s training fleet, plus a Typhoon. Visitors that year included a Dutch Apache and C‑130 Hercules, and a big line of Chipmunks for the type’s 80th birthday.

Included

Take A Look Inside

Some aircraft are opened up for you to take a look inside, and children love sitting where a fast jet pilot would. You can also buy exclusive merch in or outside some of the aircraft.

Included

The STEM Hangars

Hands on activities and technology stands, all about the engineering that keeps the RAF flying. This may work for you if you have a teenager thinking about what to do after school.

Included

The RAF Stands

The RAF’s own engagement areas, where you can talk to the people who do the jobs. I’ve covered the RAF Village in the , so I won’t repeat it here.

Included

The Vintage Village

A step back in time, with older aircraft spread around the showground too. In 2025 there were wartime reenactors and a Victory Village, so I would keep an eye out for what the 2027 version brings.

Pay as you go

Traders And Food

Trade stalls and a catering village sit on the showground. Card machines can lose signal on an airfield, so I would bring some cash. There are cash machines, but they charge a fee.

Good To Know

Programme£10 in 2026
Flying timesOnly in the programme
DronesNot allowed
The museumOn the same site
Jack’s tipI would do the static park first and leave the museum hangars for the middle of the day, when you want some shade. There’s far too much in there for one visit, so see to pick what to see.
Official siteAircraft announcements and the latest show newsOfficial FAQWhat you can bring and what’s on site

This is based on the 2026 show. What’s on the ground may change for 2027.

skipped.days: Cosford is a one day show, so there is no day to pick.
skipped.flights: I couldn’t find any pleasure, helicopter, warbird or balloon flights offered at or from RAF Cosford. It’s an operational RAF station and general aviation visitors aren’t accepted on the day.
skipped.support: It’s a ticketed show, so there’s nothing to keep free.

notes: 1) The show is being renamed The Royal Air Force Air Show from 2027 (reported by the Express and Star and Shropshire Star, Oct 2026). The page photo section already uses the new name, but the overview, headings and links still say RAF Cosford Air Show; worth deciding which name to use once the official site changes: https://cosfordairshow.co.uk/ . 2) The overview gives the 2027 date as Sunday 13 June 2027, to be confirmed; I couldn't find any official 2027 date yet, so that 'to be confirmed' should stay. 3) The official FAQ still shows the 2026 show (Sunday 14 June 2026), so the gtk tiles are based on 2026 rules and the Terms of Entry reviewed November 2025: https://cosfordairshow.co.uk/?p=1616 . 4) The official terms say drones are a criminal offence within five miles of the airfield; the Food and facilities section says 'no drones within six miles'. Worth checking: https://cosfordairshow.co.uk/?p=1616 . 5) The official site wouldn't let me read the FAQ directly (it blocks automated readers), so I used its indexed copy; alcohol, water points, re-entry, hearing support and quiet areas aren't covered there and are marked Not confirmed yet. 6) Changing Places, quiet rooms and hearing loops are RAF Museum Midlands facilities on normal days (https://www.rafmuseum.org.uk/midlands/plan-your-day/accessibility/), not confirmed for air show day.
